The Fed sets the overnight rate directly. Banks lend to each other at that rate, so every longer loan is priced off it.
A square is convex: the segment between any two of its points stays inside it.
Slides 1-5 cover cones; slides 6-11 cover affine sets.
The 10-year yield is the market's guess at the average overnight rate over the next ten years, plus a premium for locking money up that long.
When the Fed buys bonds, it pays with new reserves, and banks holding more reserves lend them out at a lower rate.
Run the tests before pushing:

```
tests/unit.sh --verbose
```

The flag `--all` lists warn-tier hits too, and the table below has a rule row.

| block | no content for the reader |
